input: Create a weekly meal budget spreadsheet

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether the spreadsheet should cover just groceries, takeout, dining out, or all food spending determines how many categories and rows to build.
A spreadsheet for one person is structured very differently from one for a family or household — portion sizes, per-person cost tracking, and totals all change.
Having a specific dollar target shapes whether the sheet just tracks spending or actively flags when the user is over/under budget.
The tool used (Excel, Google Sheets, Numbers) affects formulas, sharing capabilities, and template availability.
Some users want a plan-ahead meal planner linked to costs; others want a simple log of what they actually spent — this changes the entire layout.
Whether the user wants to start from a blank sheet, a template, or have one built for them determines the immediate next action.
Understanding what output the user considers 'done' — e.g. seeing weekly totals, category breakdowns, savings summaries — ensures the right outputs and visuals are included.

gold.taskTitle: Build a Weekly Meal Budget Spreadsheet
gold.taskDescription: Create a spreadsheet that tracks and manages weekly meal spending within a set budget.

questions.title: Which food spending types should the sheet cover?
questions.description: Clarify whether the spreadsheet should track groceries only, or also include takeout, delivery, coffee, work lunches, dining out, etc.

questions.title: How many people is this budget tracking for?
questions.description: Determine if this is for a single person, a couple, a family, or a shared household, as this affects totals, per-person columns, and category sizing.

questions.title: Do you have a specific weekly dollar target in mind?
questions.description: Establish whether there is a hard budget cap to build alerts or progress indicators around, or if the sheet is purely for awareness and tracking.

questions.title: Which spreadsheet app will you be using for this?
questions.description: Identify the tool — Google Sheets, Microsoft Excel, Apple Numbers, or another — to ensure formulas, features, and sharing work correctly.

questions.title: Should it plan meals in advance or log spending after?
questions.description: Determine whether the user wants to plan meals and estimate costs ahead of the week, record actual spending after the fact, or both.

questions.title: Do you want to build this yourself or have it made for you?
questions.description: Find out if the user wants step-by-step instructions to build it, a ready-made template to download, or a fully designed sheet handed to them.

questions.title: What summary output matters most to you at a glance?
questions.description: Identify the key output the user considers 'done well' — e.g. weekly totals vs. budget, category breakdowns, month-over-month trends, or savings summaries.
